research_notes:
Drafted 2026-10-20 by automated research; sources as listed.
REGISTRATION: Zimbabwe appears to have no statutory register of political parties (ZESN/Masunungure study 'Regulation of Political Parties Zimbabwe', Aug 2006: no law requires parties to register; parties only need candidate nominations to contest elections). Not confirmed in a current official source; verify against the Electoral Act [Chapter 2:13] before publishing the bracketed registration text.
LEGAL NAME / FOUNDING: the constitution copy used is the June 2005 version (OCR text spells 'Partriotic'); later amendments (reported 2014, 2017, 2022 and a 2026 term-extension push) were not reachable. year_founded 1987 = Unity Accord of 22 Dec 1987 creating the united ZANU (PF); the party traces its origin to ZANU founded in 1963 (encyclopedic/press sources only) - verifier to decide which year the register should show.
LEADER: name and title taken from the party's own conference resolutions (Oct 2024) as reproduced by Open Parly, plus the ZEC 2023 nomination notice for the full name. Master's Secretary General is outdated: AllAfrica, 23 Sep 2025 ('Mnangagwa Reshuffles Top Party Officials', press, quoting a party statement) reports Jacob Francis Nzwidamilimo Mudenda moved from Treasurer General to Secretary General, Patrick Chinamasa to Treasurer General, Obert Mpofu redeployed to Secretary for ICT; Christopher Mutsvangwa spokesperson/Secretary for Information and Publicity. Press only - not entered.
OFFICIAL SITE / CHANNELS: zanupf.org.zw (from master) could not be opened or found in search results, so domains and social accounts are left empty. Herald, 6 May 2014 ('Where is Zanu-PF website', press) described www.zanupf.org.zw as badly outdated. Fake ZANU-PF X/Twitter accounts have circulated (2017 BBC case, press), so handles need verification on the party's own site.
STATE FUNDING (lead, not entered): Political Parties (Finance) Act [Chapter 2:11] (Act 4 of 2001; ZimLII https://old.zimlii.org/zw/legislation/act/2001/4) funds parties with at least 5% of the vote and bans foreign donations. Press (AllAfrica 3 Sep 2025; Zambian Observer 3 Sep 2025; Open Parly 7 Jan 2026) reports General Notice 1829 of 2025, Government Gazette Extraordinary of 2 Sep 2025, issued by Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi under s.3(2) of the Act: total ZWG 147,682,500.00 for 2025, of which ZANU PF ZWG 102,343,972.50 (69.3%, based on its 2023 vote share) and CCC 30.7%. CITE (17 Oct 2025, citing the Elections Resource Centre factsheet) reports about US$7.3m paid to ZANU PF since the 2023 elections and that the Act has no reporting or audit requirement. Obtain GN 1829 of 2025 from the Government Gazette (Veritas / Printflow) to fill major_funders and sources_money. No party annual accounts or donor disclosures are published, so revenue_mix is empty.
SISTER BODIES (lead, not entered): the constitution provides for party enterprises and party publications edited by the Secretary for Information and Publicity, but names none. ZESN 2006 names M&S Syndicate as the party's business holding; the party weekly 'The Voice'/'The People's Voice' and Zidco Holdings are known from press/encyclopedic sources only. No official company-register access (Zimbabwe's companies registry is not publicly searchable online).
PARENT GROUP: no membership of Socialist International or another formal international party family was found; the six-party Southern African liberation-movements grouping (often called Former Liberation Movements of Southern Africa, FLMSA) is informal - verifier to decide whether it belongs in parent_group.
Master claims (state-party fusion, links to ZBC, Zimpapers, military, Tshabangu) are not official-record facts and were not entered. Moved to notes before import (an informal grouping, not a party family): parent_group "Southern African former liberation movements (six-party grouping: ANC, MPLA, SWAPO, FRELIMO, ZANU-PF, CCM; annual Liberation Movements Summit)".
